★★★ THE RUNNABLE WITNESS FOR [[D-ASM-ARM64-LDR-TO-LDUR-CONVENIENCE-ALIAS-REFUSED]] (cycle P55, lane vd, 2026-09-03).

★★★ WHAT WAS WRONG. AArch64 gas spells ONE load with TWO encodings: `ldr` is the SCALED unsigned-offset form (imm12, scaled by the access size, non-negative only) and `ldur` the UNSCALED signed one (imm9, a raw byte count, -256..255). A displacement the scaled form cannot represent is NOT an error in either reference — both silently assemble `ldr` as the unscaled encoding, and NEITHER warns. DSS mapped `ldr` to the scaled opcode alone and refused every such line, loudly, at every width and on both register files. ✔MEASURED at the P55 base, gas 2.42 and clang 18.1.3 probed SEPARATELY and agreeing on all 35 cells: `ldr x0,[x1,#1]` = 0xF8401020, `str x0,[x1,#1]` = 0xF8001020, `ldr d0,[x1,#-8]` = 0xFC5F8020, `ldr q0,[x1,#-16]` = 0x3CDF0020 — each refused by DSS with A_ImmediateOperandOutOfRange.

★★★ THE ROW'S OWN PREMISE WAS NARROWER THAN THE TRUTH, AND HALF B OF THIS FILE IS THE COUNTEREXAMPLE. The row framed the trigger as *an offset that is not a multiple of the access size*. ✔MEASURED, that is not the predicate: the rewrite ALSO fires for every NEGATIVE offset even when it IS a multiple (`str x2,[x1,#-8]` — 8 divides 8), because the scaled field is UNSIGNED; and at `b` width every offset is a multiple of 1, so 'non-multiple' cannot be the trigger there at all. The real predicate is *the scaled form cannot represent this displacement* — non-negative AND a multiple AND within 4095 x accessSize.

★★★ IT IS A CONVENIENCE ALIAS, NOT A MEANING CHANGE, WHICH IS THE QUESTION THAT HAD TO BE ANSWERED BEFORE IT COULD BE IMPLEMENTED. ✔MEASURED: `ldr x0,[x1,#1]` and `ldur x0,[x1,#1]` name the same effective address (LDUR does not scale), the same access size and the same register. The two differ in ENCODING and never in what the program does — which is exactly the scaled-vs-unscaled election DSS already performs on its own compiler-generated path (`selectFrameMemOp` swaps an out-of-imm9 frame offset onto the scaled form). Adopting it makes the hand-written surface agree with the generated one rather than introducing a new kind of substitution.

★★★ WHY THIS FILE EXECUTES INSTEAD OF PINNING A WORD, AND IT IS THE WHOLE DESIGN. `tests/asm/test_asm_arm64_memory_dialect_rows.cpp` already asserts the emitted WORD for all 35 measured cells. What a word cannot prove is that the instruction addresses the memory the programmer NAMED — and that is precisely the risk here, because the two encodings read their displacement field differently: `ldr`'s is SCALED by the access size and `ldur`'s is a RAW byte count. An offset routed to the wrong one is not a refusal, it is a valid instruction at the WRONG ADDRESS, and 1/2/4/8/16 are exactly the multipliers involved. So each half writes through one route and reads through a SECOND, INDEPENDENTLY COMPUTED address (`add`/`sub` into a scratch register), and every destination slot is POISONED first.

★★ THE THREE HALVES ARE THREE DIFFERENT QUESTIONS, not three samples of one: (A) the LOAD direction at a non-multiple offset on the integer file; (B) the STORE direction at a negative offset that IS a multiple — the case the row's premise could not explain; (C) the SIMD&FP q form at the widest access (16 bytes) and a negative offset, which is the other register file and the largest scale factor. A fix that reached only the FP widths, or only the non-multiple case, or only one direction, fails one of them.

★★ AND THE EXIT CODE CARRIES WHICH HALF BROKE. The poisons are 100 / 200 / 300 against the correct 7 / 11 / 52: correct is 70, and a single failing half gives 163, 3 or 62 (mod 256). No combination lands back on 70, so a partial regression cannot read as a partial pass.

★ THE RED-ON-DISABLE ARM IS A BUILD FAILURE RATHER THAN A WRONG NUMBER: strip `guard.immMultipleOf` from the shipped target's scaled memory variants, or `opcodesAreRankedEncodings` from the dialect's `ldr`/`str` rows, and this file stops compiling — the encoders are already fail-loud on an unrepresentable immediate, so the pin rides the diagnostic that exists rather than a second one invented for it. Both mutants are pinned by name in the unit file.

★ THE `release` ARM, SCOPED HONESTLY. At the `encode` tier no MIR module exists, so the optimizer, the register allocator and calling-convention materialization never run — this arm does NOT witness the optimizer and cannot. It pins the narrower fact that `--config=release` still produces a working binary from assembly text.

optimizedPipelines.label: release
optimizedPipelines.$commentByteIdentical: The source of this example IS assembly, so it is assembled without ever forming the HIR/MIR an optimizer pass runs on. No pipeline can transform it and no edit to this example could make this arm differ from the baseline — the arm earns its place by pinning that naming a pipeline does not BREAK an assembly example. Deliberately NOT given "mustDifferFromBaseline": an honest no-op, not a missed opt-in.
